title: Ahmad:
headline: An Afghan peacebuilder says pain is pain, and trusted local mediators are how you heal it.
story: Ahmad leads an Afghan NGO. His lesson: every conflict is different, but pain is pain. His team picks trusted local people and teaches them to mediate. They live there, so they solve problems for good.

Then the proof. A local government said no to training 40 women. He brought religious and tribal leaders, made every trainer, cook and guard a woman, and won the project. It must feel calm, wise and hopeful.
do: Open on frame 1 on “pain is pain” with the hook text. No logo, no fade.
Keep his English exactly as he says it. Do not fix his grammar in captions.
Stay on his face for the 40-women story. It is the heart of the video.
Cover every trim with B-roll or a soft speech ramp.
Name super at 00:14, after the hook.
dont: Never name the Taliban or the Afghan government. He does not.
Do not use 07:28–08:50. It is a different video.
No camera-shutter sounds. No choppy jump cuts.
No red-lanyard people in any B-roll.

transcript:
Auto-transcript of FX6_LVH_6361.MXF (Ahmad, Brussels, 15 Sep 2026). Times are mm:ss in the source file. Every line is labelled "Interviewee" in the source. Interviewer lines here: 00:00, 00:27-00:41, 07:00. 00:04-00:24 is a false start, repeated at 00:44.
[00:00] Interviewer: Tell us about your work in Afghanistan and the most significant lesson you've learned.
[00:04] First of all, thanks for inviting me to such a valuable conference.
[00:14] Actually, I'm leading an Afghan non-governmental institution or NGO.
[00:24] It's called Cooperation Center for Afghanistan.
[00:27] Interviewer: Sorry to interrupt, but it's important that you look in the camera here, in the lens.
[00:41] Restart. Very good.
[00:44] First of all, thanks for inviting me to such a valuable conference with very important issues.
[00:59] Actually, I'm working in Afghanistan as a director of Afghan NGO.
[01:08] The base of our NGO or our activities are focused on human rights.
[01:16] So, I'm sure that today's conference, subject matters and contents are very, very relevant to human rights,
[01:29] because human rights is a wide-range meaning word.
[01:38] Through our projects, we usually maintain peace and equity and equality in judgment between our people.
[01:53] In recent years, we had the project, actually the project was conflict resolution,
[02:00] but because the topic of this project was in contact with the government institutions,
[02:09] we changed the topic of the project from conflict resolution to social cohesion, but the content was the same.
[02:26] Through this project, we achieved some unbelievable results.
[02:43] The conflict in our country is different from other countries' conflict,
[02:47] because every area has their own problems.
[02:54] If you compare to people, if I have to take, somebody might have headache.
[03:01] But one thing is common between these two people, that is age, that both have pain.
[03:11] So, in our country, usually the problems are religious issue, religious problem like language, tribal,
[03:24] and also in some economical issue like inherent in some similar things.
[03:33] But through this project, we could establish several social committees,
[03:43] and through these committees, we selected very influential, very trusted people with very good background,
[03:53] and we taught them mediation skills, how to mediate between people.
[04:02] And now, which is unbelievable that the local authorities refer, they refer some cases to our committee,
[04:15] and our committee, our completion in solving of the problem, refer it back to the government institution.
[04:24] There is a huge difference, because the people who are in our mediation committees,
[04:30] they are from the local area, they are always there, and they do some things that in the future,
[04:40] people do not blame them, and they should not be in trouble in the future.
[04:46] So, they try, they do their best to solve a problem or a case in a very peaceful way that do not harm each side.
[05:00] It means like win-win rule, that both sides should be benefited and the problem solved forever.
[05:09] Yeah, Israel and Palestine have some similarity to any problems, because before pain is pain.
[05:39] It doesn't matter that your feet has pain or your head has pain, but all your body will affected by the pain.
[05:51] Regarding the Palestine and Israel problem, we can use our experiences from our countries,
[06:06] that we should select the very new experience, trusted and neutral mediator,
[06:16] because if the mediators be like have some sympathy with one of the sides,
[06:26] so we cannot reach to a final peace process.
[06:31] So, I think and also there should be guarantee,
[06:36] it should be very strong guarantee according to the decision of this peace process,
[06:45] because if there is no guarantee, there is from big powers or neighboring countries,
[06:54] it is impossible to have a sustainable peace.
[07:00] Interviewer: I know you have experience with both levels and what you think the role needs to be to bring government and civil society together.
[07:26] Yeah, very good question.
[07:28]-[08:50] (civil society as a bridge: not used in this video)
[09:00] I give you an example.
[09:01] Last time we had a project in one of our provinces.
[09:05] The project was for livelihood and in the project, we had 40 females to be trained in tailoring.
[09:17] But the local government said, no, it should be all the men because we do not allow you to teach women.
[09:26] But we spoke to them and we took the area religious leaders and tribal leaders and went to the government,
[09:36] to the governor office and spoke to them that actually this project is designed for women, not men.
[09:45] And men are mostly busy on the field, agriculture field and even they don't have enough time to learn.
[09:55] But at home, usually our mothers, sisters and girls, they do the tailoring.
[10:02] It is important but we will provide the situation that you want.
[10:07] All the trainers will be female, also the cook, even the security guards will be women.
[10:15] And we do not allow any male to walk around and contact these trainees.
[10:23] And finally, we could persuade the local government governor to allow us to do this project.
[10:32] So, this needs some kind of skills, how to mediate, how to persuade this.
[10:41] We should have very high persuasion skills to persuade the opposite side.
[10:46] So, this piece also is like this. This was like a case.
[10:50] It does not matter that it is a political case or economical case or any kind of conflicts.
[11:00] But we can solve conflicts through good mediators and good mediation skills.
